title: Automated CI/CD Pipeline for Web Applications
description: Develop an automated CI/CD pipeline that builds, tests and deploys a sample web application whenever new code is pushed to a Git repository. The pipeline must stop deployment if the automated tests fail.
requirements: Configure a GitHub Actions workflow triggered by a code push.
Execute at least one automated test.
Deploy the application to an accessible server.
demonstration: Modify the application, push the change, and demonstrate the automated testing and deployment process.
tools: GitHub Actions, Git, Docker, Nginx, Node.js or Python.

title: Automated Code Quality Gate
description: Develop a CI workflow that checks source code for basic quality issues before allowing it to proceed to deployment. The system must run automated tests and code-quality checks and reject code that violates the configured rules.
requirements: Integrate a linter and automated tests.
Include one intentionally faulty code change.
Display the reason for a failed quality check.
Deploy the application when all checks pass.
deliverables: Evidence of a rejected faulty change.
demonstration: Push a valid change and then a faulty change. Show the pipeline passing the first and rejecting the second.
tools: GitHub Actions, ESLint or Ruff, Jest or pytest, Docker.

title: Zero-Downtime Deployment Simulator
description: Implement a blue-green deployment system that switches between two application versions while minimizing service interruption. The system must verify the health of the new version before directing traffic to it.
requirements: Configure Nginx as a reverse proxy.
Implement a script to switch between versions.
Perform a health check before switching traffic.
Retain the previous version if the new version is unhealthy.
demonstration: Send repeated requests while switching versions. Demonstrate that requests continue succeeding and that an unhealthy version is not activated.
tools: Docker Compose, Nginx, Bash, curl.

title: Automated Release Rollback System
description: Develop a deployment workflow that automatically restores the previous working application version when a newly deployed version fails its health checks.
requirements: Automatically restore the previous version after a failed health check.
deliverables: Logs showing a failed release and successful rollback.
demonstration: Deploy an intentionally unhealthy version and demonstrate that the system detects the failure and restores the previous working version.
tools: Docker, Docker Compose, Bash, Python.

title: Software Build Artifact Registry
description: Develop a workflow that generates versioned software artifacts, stores them in a designated repository, and verifies their integrity before deployment.
requirements: Assign a unique version or build identifier to each artifact.
Store the artifacts in a registry or designated artifact repository.
Retrieve a selected artifact and verify its checksum.
demonstration: Publish two versions, retrieve one version, and verify that its checksum matches the recorded value.
tools: GitHub Actions, Docker Registry or GitHub Packages, SHA-256 utilities.

title: Containerize a Legacy Application
description: Package a sample application into a Docker container so that it can run consistently without manually installing its dependencies on the host machine.
requirements: Build and run the Docker image.
Make the application accessible through a browser or API client.
deliverables: README with build and execution instructions.
demonstration: Build the image and run the application in a container. Show that it works without manually installing the application dependencies on the host.
tools: Docker, Docker Compose, Node.js or Python.

title: Self-Healing Container Platform
description: Develop a containerized application that detects failures and automatically recovers from common service interruptions.
requirements: Define an appropriate container restart policy.
Demonstrate the difference between a running container and a healthy
Record recovery events or status changes.
deliverables: Evidence of recovery after a controlled failure.
demonstration: Trigger a controlled container failure and demonstrate the recovery process.
tools: Docker, Docker Compose, Python or Node.js.

title: Kubernetes Application Deployment and Scaling
description: Deploy a containerized application to a Kubernetes environment and demonstrate replica management, health checking and automatic replacement of failed pods.
requirements: Scale the application from one to three replicas.
Demonstrate replacement of a deleted pod.
demonstration: Deploy the application, scale it to three replicas, delete one pod and demonstrate Kubernetes creating a replacement.
tools: Kubernetes, Minikube or kind, Docker, kubectl.
scopeRestriction: Teams must have a working local Kubernetes environment or access to a prepared cluster. Installing and configuring a new Kubernetes environment from scratch is not part of the challenge.

title: Container Resource Optimization
description: Build a tool that monitors container CPU and memory usage and demonstrates how resource limits affect a container running a controlled workload.
requirements: Repeat the workload and record the results.
demonstration: Run the workload, observe its resource usage, apply limits and show the resulting behavior.
tools: Docker, Python, Docker statistics, cAdvisor or Grafana.

title: Container Network Isolation
description: Create a multi-container application with restricted network communication so that each service can access only the components required for its operation.
requirements: Create a frontend, backend and database service.
Configure Docker networks to restrict communication.
deliverables: Three services or equivalent test containers.
demonstration: Show that permitted connections succeed and prohibited connections fail.
tools: Docker Compose, Docker bridge networks, curl, netcat.

title: One-Command Infrastructure Provisioning
description: Develop an Infrastructure as Code solution that provisions a small, repeatable application environment using declarative configuration.
requirements: Define at least two related infrastructure resources.
Generate and review a Terraform plan.
deliverables: README containing setup and cleanup instructions.
demonstration: Provision the environment, show the created resources and demonstrate how a configuration change affects the Terraform plan.
tools: Terraform, Docker provider or an approved cloud provider.
scopeRestriction: Local Docker resources or a prepared cloud sandbox are acceptable. Paid cloud provisioning is not mandatory.

title: Automated Linux Server Configuration
description: Automate the configuration of a Linux server using Ansible. The playbook must install a web server, configure a simple web page and ensure the service is running.
requirements: Write a playbook to install Nginx.
Verify that the page is accessible.
Demonstrate repeat execution without unnecessary changes.
demonstration: Execute the playbook, access the web page and run the playbook again to demonstrate idempotency.
tools: Ansible, Ubuntu, Nginx.

title: Automated Cloud Storage Backup and Restore
description: Develop an automated backup and restoration system that stores timestamped copies of selected files and verifies that the files can be recovered without data corruption.
requirements: Select a set of sample files.
Store backups separately from the original files.
deliverables: Backup storage directory or object storage.
Backup logs and integrity verification results.
demonstration: Back up sample files, remove a working copy, restore the files and verify that their checksums match the originals.
tools: Python or Bash, MinIO or a designated backup directory.

title: Infrastructure Configuration Drift Detector
description: Build a tool that compares a declared infrastructure configuration with the observed configuration and reports differences without automatically modifying the environment.
requirements: Define a baseline configuration using YAML or JSON.
Collect the actual state of a test environment.
deliverables: Test cases for matching and mismatching configurations.
demonstration: Modify a monitored setting, run the checker and demonstrate that it identifies the configuration drift.
tools: Python, YAML, JSON, Ansible facts or Linux configuration utilities.

title: Cloud Resource Cost Estimator
description: Develop a tool that estimates infrastructure costs using a predefined pricing dataset and compares alternative infrastructure configurations.
requirements: Allow users to select resource types and quantities.
Calculate estimated hourly and monthly costs.
demonstration: Compare two infrastructure configurations and explain which resources contribute most to their cost differences.
tools: Python or JavaScript, CSV or JSON, Streamlit or a simple web interface.
scopeRestriction: Actual cloud billing integration is not required.

title: Real-Time Server Health Dashboard
description: Develop a dashboard that displays server CPU utilization, memory usage, disk usage and uptime, helping administrators identify resource problems.
requirements: Collect metrics from a Linux server.
Display CPU, memory and disk usage.
Configure at least two warning thresholds.
Show changing metrics under a controlled workload.
Deploy the dashboard to an accessible server.
demonstration: Generate CPU or memory load and show the corresponding changes on the dashboard.
tools: Python, Flask, psutil, Prometheus and Grafana.

title: Alerting and Incident Notification System
description: Build a monitoring system that detects service failures and generates notifications containing the affected service, detected condition and time of occurrence.
requirements: Monitor a service or application endpoint.
Generate notifications through email, a webhook or a local receiver.
Include useful incident information in each alert.
demonstration: Stop a monitored service, demonstrate an alert, restart the service and show that recovery is detected.
tools: Python, HTTP health checks, Prometheus and Alertmanager, or a local webhook receiver.

title: Centralized Log Search Platform
description: Develop a centralized logging solution that collects logs from at least two application services and allows users to search and filter them through a common interface.
requirements: Create or use two sample services.
Store or aggregate the logs centrally.
Filter logs by service and severity.
Demonstrate investigation of a sample error.
demonstration: Generate errors in both services and retrieve the relevant logs from the same interface.
tools: Grafana Loki, Grafana, Docker Compose.
scopeRestriction: Use predefined logging configurations where possible. Building a complete production logging platform is not required.

title: Automated Root-Cause Analysis Assistant
description: Develop a diagnostic assistant that analyzes application logs and health-check results to identify likely causes of common operational failures and recommend investigation steps.
requirements: Accept logs or structured incident data.
Implement rules for at least four failure scenarios.
Identify the likely cause of each scenario.
Display the evidence supporting each diagnosis.
Test the assistant against multiple incident examples.
demonstration: Provide different incident datasets and demonstrate how the assistant produces diagnoses supported by the input evidence.
tools: Python, regular expressions, JSON.
scopeRestriction: A rule-based solution is sufficient. An LLM integration is optional.

title: Service Availability and SLA Reporter
description: Build a monitoring tool that periodically checks a service endpoint and calculates its availability, downtime and response-time statistics.
requirements: Calculate availability percentage and observed downtime.
demonstration: Run successful and failed health checks against a test service and generate a report showing the resulting availability.
tools: Python, SQLite, HTTP client libraries.

title: Automated Container Vulnerability Scanner
description: Create an automated workflow that scans container images for known vulnerabilities and prevents images exceeding a configured severity threshold from proceeding to deployment.
requirements: Scan the image using a vulnerability scanner.
Generate a report of detected vulnerabilities.
Integrate the scanner into a CI workflow or equivalent automated pipeline.
deliverables: Evidence of a passing and failing scan.
demonstration: Scan an appropriate training image, demonstrate the configured policy and show how an updated image changes the result.
tools: Trivy, Docker, GitHub Actions.

title: Secret Leak Detection in Git Repositories
description: Develop a secret-detection workflow that identifies dummy credentials accidentally introduced into source code and prevents the affected change from passing the configured security checks.
requirements: Integrate scanning into a pre-commit hook or CI workflow.
Report the affected file and detected issue.
Demonstrate detection of a dummy credential.
deliverables: README explaining safe secret handling and remediation.
demonstration: Attempt to commit a dummy API key and demonstrate that the scanner detects or rejects the change.
tools: Gitleaks, Git hooks, GitHub Actions.

title: Infrastructure Security Compliance Checker
description: Develop a security-checking workflow that evaluates Infrastructure as Code configurations against a small set of predefined security policies.
requirements: Create compliant and noncompliant sample configurations.
Define at least three security policies.
Configure a validation gate that rejects a critical violation.
deliverables: Evidence of successful validation after correction.
demonstration: Scan a configuration with an overly permissive access rule, demonstrate the violation, correct the configuration and rerun the checker.
tools: Checkov or OPA/Conftest, Terraform, GitHub Actions.

title: Automated Linux Security Baseline Auditor
description: Build a read-only auditing tool that evaluates a Linux machine against a small set of security baseline checks and recommends corrective actions for failed checks.
requirements: Implement at least five security checks.
Report passed, failed and unverified checks.
Explain why each failed check matters.
demonstration: Run the auditor against a test Linux machine and display the results of at least three checks.
tools: Bash or Python, OpenSSH configuration, systemd, Linux file permissions.

title: Software Supply Chain Verification
description: Develop an artifact-integrity verification workflow that calculates a checksum during a build and verifies the artifact before deployment.
requirements: Store the checksum alongside artifact metadata.
deliverables: Test evidence for successful and failed verification.
demonstration: Verify an untouched artifact, modify a copy and demonstrate that the altered artifact fails verification.
tools: Python or Bash, SHA-256, GitHub Actions.

title: Automated Network and Service Diagnostics
description: Develop a diagnostic tool that checks network and application connectivity and provides troubleshooting suggestions based on the observed results.
requirements: Accept a hostname, IP address or service endpoint.
Check HTTP response status and response time.
Provide troubleshooting suggestions for failed checks.
deliverables: Test cases covering healthy and failing endpoints.
demonstration: Test a working service and a controlled failing service, then compare the diagnostic results.
tools: Python, socket, dig, HTTP client libraries.

title: Reverse Proxy and Load Balancer
description: Deploy two backend application instances behind a reverse proxy that distributes incoming requests and continues serving requests when one backend becomes unavailable.
requirements: Configure Nginx as a reverse proxy.
Identify which backend handled each request.
Test the system with one backend unavailable.
demonstration: Send repeated requests, demonstrate distribution across both backends, stop one backend and verify that requests continue reaching the available backend.
tools: Nginx, Docker Compose, Python or Node.js.

title: Local DNS Management and Health Checker
description: Create a DNS validation tool that compares actual DNS resolution results with a predefined list of expected hostnames and IP addresses.
requirements: Define at least three expected DNS records.
Configure a local DNS service or use a predefined DNS test environment.
deliverables: Report identifying valid and invalid records.
README with setup and testing instructions.
demonstration: Validate several records, introduce an incorrect mapping in the test environment and demonstrate that the checker detects the mismatch.
tools: CoreDNS or BIND9, Python, dig.
scopeRestriction: A predefined DNS environment or simulated record dataset is acceptable if local DNS configuration becomes an environmental obstacle.

title: Network Configuration Drift Monitor
description: Develop a tool that compares the current network configuration of a Linux machine with an approved baseline and reports unexpected changes.
requirements: Capture expected interface addresses, routes and DNS settings.
demonstration: Capture the baseline, change a test setting and run the checker to identify the difference.
tools: Python, Linux iproute2, JSON.

title: Firewall Rule Audit and Generator
description: Build a tool that audits a declared firewall policy, identifies overly permissive rules and generates a proposed corrected configuration for review.
requirements: Accept a firewall policy in JSON or YAML.
Define at least three validation rules.
Report each violation and its severity.
demonstration: Audit a sample policy containing unnecessary access, show the findings and generate a more restrictive configuration.
tools: Python, YAML or JSON, UFW or nftables in a test environment.

title: Automated Development Environment Setup Wizard
description: Develop a setup tool that checks prerequisites, prepares a sample application's environment and launches the application with minimal manual configuration.
requirements: Check whether required tools are installed.
Create a configuration file from a safe template.
Provide a repeatable setup or launch command.
Avoid overwriting existing configuration without permission.
demonstration: Run the setup workflow in a prepared test environment and demonstrate that it checks prerequisites and launches the application.
tools: Python or Bash, Git, Docker Compose.

title: Deployment Approval and Audit Portal
description: Develop a lightweight portal that records deployment requests, approval decisions, version identifiers and deployment outcomes.
requirements: Store requests in a persistent database.
Implement pending, approved and rejected states.
Trigger a predefined deployment script or a safe simulated deployment.
demonstration: Submit a deployment request, approve it, trigger the predefined workflow and inspect the resulting audit record.
tools: FastAPI or Flask, SQLite, HTML/CSS, Docker.

title: Database Backup Verification and Recovery
description: Develop an automated workflow that backs up a sample database, restores the backup into a separate test database and verifies that the restored data matches the original.
requirements: Restore it into a separate test database.
Compare record counts or selected records.
demonstration: Create a backup, restore it into a clean test database and demonstrate that the restored records match the original dataset.
tools: MySQL or PostgreSQL, Bash or Python, Docker.

title: Deployment Performance Benchmarking Tool
description: Build a benchmarking tool that measures and compares the performance of two application versions under the same workload.
requirements: Prepare two distinguishable application versions or configurations.
deliverables: Comparison report with charts or a table.
demonstration: Run the same workload against both versions and display the resulting performance differences.
tools: k6 or Locust, Python, CSV, Matplotlib.

title: Self-Service DevOps Deployment Portal
description: Develop a web portal through which an authorized user can select a predefined application, choose a supported configuration and initiate a deployment workflow.
requirements: Create a web interface for selecting one application.
Provide two or three predefined configuration options.
Validate deployment requests on the backend.
Display queued, running, successful or failed status.
Display the deployed application's endpoint or a useful failure message.
demonstration: Select the sample application, initiate deployment through the portal, monitor the deployment status and open the resulting application.
tools: FastAPI or Flask, Docker Compose, SQLite.
scopeRestriction: Support only one application and a small set of predefined configurations. Do not implement arbitrary shell-command execution or a general- purpose deployment platform.
